title: Christie's acquires leading British auction house Dreweatts
summary: Christie's announces that it is acquiring the UK auction house Dreweatts in a move that will enable growth opportunities for both houses and offer their clients an enhanced service. Dreweatts auction house, established in 1759, is one of the foremost auction houses in the UK and holds more than 70 specialist sales each year across many categories including single owner collections and house sales. It runs from its main saleroom, Donnington Priory in Newbury, Berkshire. Bonnie Brennan, Christie's CEO, said: "This is an exciting moment for Christie's and Dreweatts. We have long admired Dreweatts as a best-in-class business, with particular strength in a part of the market that is highly complementary to our own. Most importantly, our clients collect across categories and at every price point, and together we have the opportunity to provide them with an even broader and more complete level of service. Both businesses will continue to operate much as they do today, while building on their

title: Roy Lichtenstein: Like New offers a fresh look at the artist who transformed the language of modern painting
summary: Few artists have created a visual language as immediately recognizable as Roy Lichtenstein. His bold outlines, brilliant primary colors, comic-book imagery, and signature Ben-Day dots have become so deeply embedded in contemporary culture that it is easy to overlook just how revolutionary they once were. Roy Lichtenstein: Like New , an impressive new publication accompanying the Whitney Museum of American Art's major retrospective, offers a welcome opportunity to rediscover the artist beyond the familiar images that made him famous. Authored by artist Alex Da Corte and Whitney curator Meg Onli, with contributions from Dan Nadel, Marshall N. Price, and Carmen Winant, this beautifully illustrated, 366-page hardcover makes a persuasive case for reconsidering Lichtenstein as far more than a painter who elevated comic strips into fine art. title: Phil Collins lyrics fetch $51.2K at King's Trust Auction
summary: Julien’s Auctions announces the results of The King’s Trust 50th Anniversary Auction Featuring the Phil Collins Archive. The special benefit sale marked 50 years of The King’s Trust, a charity helping young people facing adversity develop the confidence and skills they need to move into work, education or training. Held on Thursday, November 19, in Los Angeles, the sale attracted fans and collectors from around the world. Alongside an extraordinary collection of items from Phil Collins, who was recently inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame as a solo artist, the auction featured contributions from music legends including Sir Paul McCartney, Sir Elton John, Sir Mick Jagger, Annie Lennox, Mark Knopfler, Sir Brian May, The Who, Muse and more. title: SJ Auctioneers announces online-only Collectible Collections for the Holiday Season auction
summary: The holidays are fast approaching, and with them comes the often-agonizing question as to what to get those special people on one’s last-minute holiday gift list. Luckily, there’s a one-stop shop for nearly everyone on that list, young and old. It’s SJ Auctioneers’ online-only Collectible Collections for the Holiday Season auction, open for bidding now and ending on Sunday, December 20th. The auction, beginning at 6pm Eastern Time, features 462 lots in a wide range of collecting categories. These include vintage games (including mahjong designer games by Piaget and Porsche), toys, Swarovski and Herend figures, vintage pens, Baccarat pieces, sterling silver flatware sets and objects, and wonderful decorative items. title: The Dalí Foundation presents the second issue of Dalí News, devoted to the relationship between art and fashion
summary: On November 23, the Gala-Salvador Dalí Foundation presented the second volume of Dalí News at the Dalí Theatre-Museum in Figueres. An annual journal with an international scope, it takes as its starting point the publishing venture created by Salvador Dalí in the 1940s, reviving its critical, visionary and interdisciplinary spirit to engage with contemporary thought. The second issue is devoted to the relationship between art and fashion. It revisits one of the artist's most surprising predictions, "musical rhinoceros shoes", and sets it in dialogue with contemporary trends. title: Thelma Golden to step down as Director and Chief Curator of the Studio Museum in Harlem in late 2027
summary: Kathryn C. Chenault, Chair of the Board of Trustees of the Studio Museum in Harlem, today announced that with profound admiration for Thelma Golden, Ford Foundation Director and Chief Curator, and gratitude for her unparalleled achievements, the Board has accepted her plan to hand off leadership of the Museum in late 2027. Golden informed the Board of her decision one year after marking her 20th anniversary as the institution’s Director and Chief Curator and celebrating the opening of the historic project she spearheaded, the Museum’s first purpose-built home. Chenault announced that the Board has formed a search committee to identify a successor to Golden, retaining an international executive search firm to assist in the effort. Golden has agreed to continue leading the Museum until a successor is hired, and she will assist in ensuring a smooth transition. Kathryn C. title: MAXXI brings Futurism into dialogue with contemporary artistic research
summary: A time machine capable of transporting the Futurists into the future they had imagined—that is, our present—reinterpreting their intuitions in light of today's possibilities and contradictions: this is Sensing the Future, an exhibition curated by Gabriele Simongini that brings the visions of Futurism into dialogue with contemporary artistic research. On view at Spazio Extra MAXXI from November 25, 2026, to January 31, 2027, the exhibition examines recent technological developments and the construction of the future through a dialogue between historical works and artistic experimentation. Works by Giacomo Balla, Umberto Boccioni, Tullio Crali, De Pistoris, Fortunato Depero, Gerardo Dottori, Filippo Tommaso Marinetti and Růžena Zátková are presented alongside the research and new productions of three contemporary artists: Fabio Giampietro, Donato Piccolo and Quayola. title: Tate Liverpool to reopen in autumn 2027 with landmark Surrealism exhibition
summary: Following a £30 million redevelopment, the transformed Tate Liverpool will open to the public in autumn 2027. The gallery announced today that its reopening programme will include the first ever exhibition to explore surrealism’s relationship with the performing arts. Bringing together iconic paintings and sculptures alongside costumes, masks and films, this landmark show will offer a fresh perspective on surrealism’s enduring influence. It will also reconnect with Tate Liverpool’s original opening in 1988, when an exhibition of surrealist works from Tate’s collection inaugurated the new gallery spaces. From autumn 2027 to spring 2028, Surrealism: Staging Dream Worlds will showcase radical artists from the 1920s to 1990s – including Salvador Dalí, Eileen Agar and Man Ray – who surprised audiences with theatrical creations and surreal live acts. title: Inlaid marble slab found beneath Taj Mahal heads to Lyon & Turnbull auction
summary: A rare and beautiful Indian marble slab found in an underground room beneath the Taj Mahal by Colonel Pownoll Phipps, the British Superintendent of historic Buildings in Agra, India is coming to sale with auction house Lyon & Turnbull. Colonel Pownoll Phipps was permitted to keep it and it has remained in his family for 200 years. It now comes to auction with Lyon & Turnbull auctioneers in London and online on 9th December 2026 as a highlight of the Islamic and Indian Art sale. The 55.8cm x 45.2cm x 3cm. slab is estimated to sell for £20,000 to £30,000. During Colonel Pownoll Phipps time in this greatest of Mughal cities, he was responsible for the care of the Taj Mahal and other historic buildings. He took this job most seriously and was at times called upon to prevent damage by Europeans looking for keepsakes. title: Zayed National Museum marks first anniversary with opening of first temporary exhibition
summary: Zayed National Museum, the national museum of the United Arab Emirates, will mark its first anniversary alongside the nation's 55th Eid Al Etihad with a four-day programme of performances, tours, workshops and family activities from 1 to 4 December. Our Story Brings Us Together: Eid Al Etihad and Zayed National Museum’s First Anniversary will present a four-day programme celebrating the traditions and shared experiences that connect communities across the UAE. Visitors can enjoy traditional performances, participate in workshops and masterclasses, join specially curated tours and create new memories with family and friends. Highlights include a drone show, an aerial display by Fursan Al Emarat and a parade by Abu Dhabi Police Music Band. Adding to the celebrations, visitors can discover Tracks Through Time: The Camel in Society, Trade and Art, Zayed National Museum’s first temporary exhibition, opening on 3 December. title: Billy Joel motorcycle collection roars past estimates
summary: Global collector car market leader Gooding Christie's, the official auction house of the inaugural Retromobile New York, today conducted the historic sale of the Billy Joel Motorcycle Collection at the world-famous Javits Center, presenting 69 lots from the personal collection of the multiple Grammy and Tony Award recipient. Not only did 100% of lots sell well above their pre-auction estimates, but a remarkable portion achieved final sales prices at 5, 8, or 10 times their estimated values. This was most evident with the top lot of the auction, the 1978 Triumph Bonneville T140 'Madison Square Garden' Custom, which sold for $577,000 – over 50 times its low estimate. The Triumph was gifted to Mr. Joel on the occasion of his 150th sold-out show at Madison Square Garden. To this day, he still holds the record for most sold-out shows at New York City's premier arena. Overall, the collection generated more than $2 million in sales, surpassing

title: Andreas Herzau's photographs capture the unseen world of the Bamberg Symphony at Villa Dessauer
summary: How do you photograph music? How can a camera capture something that exists in sound, disappears almost as quickly as it is created, and leaves behind little more than an emotional impression? These questions lie at the heart of "Lichtakkord," an exhibition currently on view at Villa Dessauer in Bamberg, Germany, presenting the remarkable photographic work of Andreas Herzau (1962–2024). Running through February 28, 2027, the exhibition explores the photographer's nearly decade-long relationship with the Bamberg Symphony, offering an unconventional portrait of the internationally acclaimed orchestra as it celebrates its 80th anniversary. Rather than simply documenting musicians performing onstage, Herzau sought to capture what makes an orchestra come alive: the moments of anticipation before a concert, the gestures of musicians immersed in their work, the atmosphere of unfamiliar cities, and the quiet intervals that punctuate life on the road. title: Kaifan Wang explores bodily chaos and the surrender of artistic control in new Hong Kong show
summary: Kiang Malingue presents Spasm, Kaifan Wang's first solo exhibition with the gallery at its Hong Kong location. Wang has created more than a dozen paintings in 2026 that confront the physical, psychological and artistic dimensions of losing control—allowing spastic forces to reshape agency itself, divesting it of subjectivity, stability and semblance of autonomy. Born in Hohhot in 1996 and based in Berlin, Wang works with overflowing paint through smearing, spilling, and erasing. His surfaces resemble chromatic reactions—bubbly, volatile—or intricate remains touched by natural forces such as wind, sand, and time. In large-scale works, he builds and layers mostly with sponges, only to later erase the marks, creating space as Chinese calligraphic compositions do: through nuanced absence. title: Irish Museum of Modern Art opens a major survey of contemporary Palestinian art
summary: The Irish Museum of Modern Art (IMMA) presents A Sea for Borrowed Time, a major exhibition of contemporary Palestinian art in partnership with Sharjah Art Foundation. Drawing its title from the poetry of Mahmoud Darwish, this exhibition brings together artistic practices that reflect on continuity in the face of displacement, and the enduring relationship between people and place. Bringing together works by Tarek Al-Ghoussein, Basma Al Sharif, Simone Fattal, Shadi Habib Allah, Rula Halawani, Hazem Harb, Khalil Rabah and Abdul Hay Mosallam Zarara – the exhibition examines how contemporary artists have responded to the Israeli occupation of Palestinian territories. title: Dana Awartani reconstructs destroyed Middle Eastern heritage sites in new Lisson show
summary: For her first exhibition with Lisson, Dana Awartani builds on significant recent presentations at Arnolfini, Towner Eastbourne and the Venice Biennale, with a new body of floor-based sculptures and paintings on paper. Four installations continue the series of mosaics made for the National Pavilion of Saudi Arabia at the 61st Venice Biennale (ends 22 November), entitled May your tears never dry, you who weep over stones. These iterations of her handmade, brick tile floors restore now lost decorative mosaics from former sites of worship or architectural importance that were destroyed over the past three or four years, continuing her exploration and preservation of destroyed sites of cultural heritage in the wider Arab world. title: Carrie Yamaoka named recipient of the 2026 Trellis Stepping Stone Grant
summary: Kiang Malingue shared that Carrie Yamaoka is a recipient of the 2026 Trellis Stepping Stone grant. Trellis Art Fund is a private foundation that supports the work of individual artists through grantmaking and professional development. Founded in 2024, Trellis’s Stepping Stone grant program awards artists with promising artistic practices. Each grantee will receive $40,000 in installments over two years, with a total of $800,000 awarded across the 2026 cohort. Stepping Stone Grantees are selected by an anonymous jury from a nomination pool of more than 131 artists eligible to work in the United States, nominated by more than 65 curators, historians, artists, and other art-world professionals from across the country. title: Conrad Shawcross debuts 'Time Pebble' sculptures and immersive 'Slow Arc' works at Victoria Miro
summary: Victoria Miro is presenting Shadows of the Mechanism, an exhibition by Conrad Shawcross comprising the debut of a significant new body of work, Time Pebble, and an immersive, multi-sensory installation of the artist’s acclaimed series, Slow Arc inside a Cube. ‘I have long been fascinated and beguiled by time, and am always excited by the way the relentless march of contemporary science is constantly constructing and eroding our realities. With this new series I have strived to find a way to geometrically envision notions of the very early universe’ – Conrad Shawcross Inspired by maps and diagrams in cosmology and physics, the Time Pebble series explores the paradox of trying to conceive of the Universe from beyond itself. title: Sakshi Gallery marks 40th year with 'Drawn to the Image,' a multi-venue show in Baroda
summary: Is the image now banal? Beginning with this provocation, Drawn to the Image, curated by Atul Bhalla, brings together over 30 artists and more than 100 works across three venues in Baroda: ARK Foundation for the Arts, Gallery White and Space Studio. The exhibition marks a special moment in Sakshi’s gallery history, as part of its 40th year, affirming its longstanding engagement with Baroda, and the vibrant artistic communities that have shaped and continue to shape artistic practice and pedagogy in India. The exhibition begins with the contemporary condition of visual saturation, in which the constant barrage of images leaves little room for pause or contemplation. title: National Gallery of Arts of Albania launches programme under the direction of Adela Demetja
summary: An exhibition series for mid-career Albanian artists marks the Gallery’s return ahead of the reopening of its expanded building in summer 2027. The National Gallery of Arts of Albania returns to the public with a new series of solo exhibitions by mid-career Albanian artists. It begins with My heart stops missing a beat, every time!, a new anamorphic video installation by Lek M. Gjeloshi (b. 1987), opening on November 29, at HangArt, Tirana. Curated by Adela Demetja, the series is the first major initiative under her direction. Appointed in September 2025, Demetja is the first woman to lead the institution in its 72-year history. The programme invites significant positions in contemporary Albanian art to develop new commissions. It will unfold at HangArt, a temporary venue in the Kinostudio complex made available by the Ministry of Tourism, Culture

title: Syotatsu and Kansai Noguchi explore nature, tradition, and materiality in Mendes Wood DM exhibition
summary: Syotatsu and Kansai Noguchi reach past the act of artistic creation itself, each in his own way opening a dialogue with nature and with traditional artistic practices. In their work, permanence shows itself both in how the pieces are conceived – through physical and spiritual contact with the surroundings – and in the pursuit of a lasting presence, inscribed in the materiality of what they make even as it reinvents allegories. The exhibition presents ceramics by Kansai Noguchi and paintings by Syotatsu that bring this reflection to the Barra Funda space in series made from a range of natural materials, most of them from the places where the artists live. Syotatsu (b. 1982, Wakayama, Japan) began his artistic career at nineteen on the streets of Kyoto, drawing nigaoe portraits – caricatures that set out to “capture” the most striking expression of the human face.

title: Christie's New York achieves more than $1 billion in six days of cross-category sales
summary: On Monday, November 23, Christie's New York concluded a phenomenal week of strong sales across categories, achieving more than $1 billion on nearly 900 lots sold of best-in-class examples of Old Master Painting & Sculptures, Impressionist, Modern, Post-War & Contemporary Art, Design, and Classic Cars and Motorcycles. 20th/21st Century Art sales began Tuesday November 17, and closed Monday November 23—totaling $974 million across five live and two online auctions. Sales saw active participation globally, with bidders from 55 countries across Americas, EMEA and APAC, with 6% increase from the Asia-Pacific region in the 20th Century Evening Sale, the headlining sale of the season. 20th/21st Century Art Sales followed a 10-day exhibition at the auction house's Rockefeller Center flagship location from November

title: Christie's presents Important Watches during New York Luxury Week
summary: Christie's December 2026 Luxury Week will feature an exceptional selection of rare and important timepieces, led by a unique Patek Philippe Dual-Time wristwatch Reference 3452/1 by Louis Cottier, circa 1961 (Estimate: $800,000–1,600,000). Taking place on December 4 at Rockefeller Center, the Important Watches live auction brings together extraordinary vintage discoveries, exceptional modern complications, and innovative contemporary watchmaking. The carefully curated selection celebrates the artistry, heritage, and technical ingenuity of the world's most prestigious watchmakers, including Patek Philippe, Rolex, Audemars Piguet, Cartier, and A. Lange & Söhne, alongside coveted independent makers such as F.P. Journe, Richard Mille, Ferdinand Berthoud, and Kari Voutilainen. This New York auction follows a landmark season

title: Centro Botín unveils 2027 programme with collection exhibition curated by Juan Uslé
summary: Centro Botín puts the spotlight on the Fundación Botín Art Collection and the institution’s longstanding commitment to supporting art and artists. At the heart of its 2027 programme is a major exhibition drawn from the collection, occupying, for the first time, the entire west wing of the building: two floors with a combined exhibition space of 2,500 square metres. The choice of Juan Uslé as curator is no coincidence: the internationally renowned artist from Cantabria has maintained a close relationship with Fundación Botín for more than four decades, ever since he presented the series Los trabajos y los días. Las tentaciones del pintor [Work and Days: The Temptations of the Painter], one of his first solo exhibitions, at the foundation’s headquarters on Calle Pedrueca in Santander in 1984. title: Court Barn celebrates 20th anniversary with programme of exhibitions and events throughout 2027
summary: Marking two decades since it first welcomed visitors, Court Barn Museum will mark its 20th anniversary and 125 years of the Guild of Handicraft in Chipping Campden with a year-long programme of exhibitions and events throughout 2027. A highlight of the year will be a major new exhibition – Simplicity or Splendour - shining a spotlight on Alan Crawford, a driving force behind the opening of Court Barn. Celebrations will culminate with Making It! a major arts and crafts weekend festival seeking to inspire, inform and involve a new generation of talented artisans. Hosted by the art historian, writer and broadcaster, Dr James Fox, it will feature leading voices in contemporary arts and crafts, along with some of Britain’s best known cultural commentators and art historians.
